<!-- file: craft/seo-performance.md -->

## SEO and Discoverability

Animated sites often fail SEO because content hides behind JavaScript. Don't let that happen.

- **Content is in the HTML.** All text exists in server-rendered markup in its final state; animations start *from* it. Pinned chapters keep their text in the DOM.
- **One `<title>` (≤ 60 chars) and one meta description (≤ 155 chars) per page**, written for people.
- **Open Graph and Twitter cards** with a designed 1200×630 image for every main page.
- **Structured data (JSON-LD)** that matches the category: `Organization`, `Person`, `Product`/`Offer`, `Hotel`, `Restaurant`, `Event`, `Course`, `Article`, `BreadcrumbList`.
- **Semantic headings** that describe the content, not "Welcome" or "Section 2".
- **Canonical URLs, sitemap.xml and robots.txt.**
- **`llms.txt`** at the root: a plain summary of the site and key pages, so AI assistants describe it correctly.
- **Images:** descriptive file names, `alt` text, width/height attributes.
- **Internationalisation:** `lang` on `<html>`, `hreflang` for language versions (e.g. `bn` and `en`).
- **Performance is SEO:** meet the targets in `craft/performance.md`.
- **Never claim Lighthouse or Core Web Vitals scores you didn't measure.**


---

<!-- file: gates/delivery-gate.md -->

## Delivery Gate

Run this before handing back **any** page or component. It has four parts: the measured gate, a self-critique score, the AI-default scan and the craft checklist. If anything fails, fix it and run the gate again. Two passes is normal; needing three means the concept is weak, so go back to the Thinking Sequence.

---

### Part 0: Measured gate (`scripts/gate.mjs`)

Build the page, then run the script against the built file, folder or URL:

```bash
node scripts/gate.mjs dist/index.html          # or a folder, or http://localhost:3000/
node scripts/gate.mjs --verify dist/index.html # re-scan and check the stamp written in the file
```

It runs six bounded checks in a real browser and prints numbers:

| Code | Check | Fails when |
|---|---|---|
| `c` | **Contrast** at 375, 390, 768 and 1440px, reported per width: every visible text element against the pixels actually behind it. The text is hidden, the viewport is screenshotted at each scroll position and the background is sampled. A phone layout that stacks a caption over a pale crop of the image fails at 375 even when the desktop layout passes. Each element is judged by its 10th-percentile sample (not the median), so text that sits partly on a pale image edge cannot pass on its dark half. Every element is measured at every sampled scroll position (every 0.7 viewport, every 0.15 viewport in pinned zones, plus 0/25/50/75/100% of the page and of each zone); a scroll-sequence step is judged in its active (most visible) state **and in every inactive state it rests in**, so a dimmed step at 2.1:1 fails (v2.5.0; see `craft/scroll-sequences.md`). | below 4.5:1 for body text, below 3:1 for large text (≥ 24px, or ≥ 18.66px bold) |
| `o` | **Overflow** at 375, 390, 768 and 1440px | the page scrolls sideways, or an element leaves the viewport or pushes text out of its parent by more than 1px with no clipping ancestor |
| `w` | **Long display words** at 375px: every h1–h3 and any text ≥ 32px, including decorative text | the text is wider than its box, leaves the viewport, breaks a word across lines, or splits one word across elements (e.g. "Have" + "li" on two door leaves) |
| `rm` | **Reduced motion**: the page loaded with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` | text that is visible normally is hidden, or pixels keep changing on a still page |
| `a` | **Alt and names** | an `img` has no `alt`, or a link, button, input or other focusable element has no accessible name |
| `n` | **Numbers**: every number (counters, prices, `progress`/`meter`, `aria-valuenow`) read at scroll 0, after jumping to the end, and under reduced motion, then compared with the value it settles on once scrolled into view. A value that changes by itself between two settled reads (a live ticker), or that reads as a clock (`9:02`) or sits in `<time>`, `role=timer`/`status`/`log` or `aria-live`, is listed as live and not judged. | an element is visible with a value that is later corrected: "0 hectares" before a count-up runs, a price replaced after load, a counter that never runs under reduced motion |

The output ends with a stamp line built only from those numbers:
`gate: c0 o0 w0 rm0 a0 n0 · gate/2 · <id>`. The id is a hash of what was measured on this page, so the same page gives the same id and a different page does not. `c` is the total of the per-width contrast failures. A `gate/1` stamp (five checks, contrast at 1440 only, no `n`) is rejected by `--verify`: re-run the gate and paste the new line.

**Rule: a stamp is only valid if it contains numbers produced by `scripts/gate.mjs` in the same run. A hand-written stamp is rejected.** Paste the line the script printed. Never type the numbers yourself and never copy them from an example or an earlier page. `--verify` re-scans the page and rejects any stamp whose numbers or id differ from the fresh scan, or that has no `gate:` segment at all.

**No browser, no pass.** If Playwright or Chromium is missing, the script prints `not verified — no browser` and exits with code 3. Report exactly that in the handoff (`Measured: not verified — no browser`) and leave the `gate:` segment out of the stamp. Don't write a pass you didn't measure.

The checks are bounded, and each reports what it skipped (text that was covered or never settled, elements parked off-canvas such as skip links and closed drawers). When more than 30% of text elements are skipped for contrast, the gate prints a coverage warning: the `c` count is then not a full measurement, and the skipped text needs a check by hand. A clean run means these six things were measured. It doesn't mean the page is accessible. Keyboard paths, focus order and copy still need Parts 1–3.

Exit codes: `0` pass · `1` fail · `2` stamp rejected · `3` not verified (no browser, or the scan ran past `--timeout`, default 600 s, which very tall pages such as the 36,000px component gallery can do, or the sandbox is too constrained to run the browser).

**Constrained sandboxes** (Codex CLI, small CI containers, 2-CPU machines): the gate probes the machine, and if Chromium fails to start, crashes or times out it retries once in a light footprint (one renderer process via `--renderer-process-limit=1 --no-zygote`, `--disable-gpu --disable-dev-shm-usage`, operation timeouts ×3; the checks are identical). If that fails too it prints `not verified — sandbox too constrained: <reason> (attempt 1 …; attempt 2 …; machine …)` and exits 3. Report that line verbatim; don't call the page verified. `--light` starts in the light footprint; `--timeout-ms` sets the budget. Details: `docs/adapters/codex.md`.

**Optional motion report.** `node scripts/gate.mjs --report dist/index.html` (or `--report out.html` after a target) also writes a self-contained HTML file with scroll-frame strips: 8 frames at 1440px, 8 at 375px and 8 at 1440px under reduced motion. Use it to review motion by eye, show a client, or give judges something better than one screenshot. It's off by default, doesn't change the text output, and adds nothing to the gate's numbers.

---

### Part 1: Self-critique (score 1–5)

| Axis | Question | 5 means |
|---|---|---|
| **C**oncept | Is there a clear idea, and does every section serve it? | A stranger could repeat the concept sentence after one visit |
| **H**ierarchy | Within 2 seconds, is it obvious what's first, second and third on each screen? | One focal point per screen, every time |
| **S**pecificity | Could this only belong to this brief? | Swap the logo, and it would no longer make sense |
| **R**estraint | Has everything without a job been removed? | Nothing left to cut |
| **M**otion | Does every animation pass the four questions and have fallbacks? | Motion explains, never decorates, and reduced motion is designed |
| **V**ariety | Is this structurally different from previous runs (memory log) and from the template? | Different archetype, signature, type and nav from the last 5 runs |

#### Where each number comes from

You don't type the scores. Each axis is derived from one named check, and `scripts/gate.mjs` prints the result with its trace. The question in the table above is what the axis means. The check below is how it's scored.

| Axis | Check | Source | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C** | Did the concept survive the Restraint Gate? | `DESIGN.md` → "Restraint Gate record" → `Concept survived:` | `yes` → 5 · `yes, after N change(s)` → 5 − N (min 2) · `no` (replaced) → 1 |
| **H** | 375 hierarchy test: display words fit (`w`), no overflow at 375, exactly one `h1`, no skipped heading levels, one largest text on the first 375px screen | measured by gate.mjs | 5 − issues (min 1) |
| **S** | Is the archetype/signature unique across the last 5 runs, and how similar is the structural fingerprint? | `.motomation/log.json` (via `scripts/lib.mjs` fingerprints) + the stamp's archetype, signature, tier | both new and fingerprint < 50% → 5 · < 70% → 4 · one reused or ≥ 70% → 3 · both reused → 2 · identical → 1 |
| **R** | How many things the Restraint Gate cut and logged | `DESIGN.md` → "Restraint Gate record" → `- Cut:` and `- Rejected animation:` lines | 1 + cuts + rejected animations (max 5). Four logged rejections → R5 |
| **M** | Is the tier under budget? | measured by gate.mjs against the stamp's `tier`: pinned sections ≤ 2, WebGL canvases ≤ 1, JS (gzipped) ≤ the tier budget in `craft/performance.md`, reduced motion clean (`rm0`) | 5 − budget breaches (min 1); any `rm` failure caps M at 2 |
| **V** | How many sections repeat an entrance pattern already used on the page? | measured by gate.mjs: each top-level section's entrance (fade, x, y, scale, clip, filter, or static) | 5 − repeats (min 1). Static sections don't count |

A traced stamp reads like this, with the trace in brackets after each number:
`critique: C5[restraint:kept] H4[375:1] S5[last5:archetype-new,signature-new,fp31] R5[cuts:2,anim:2] M5[t2:pins1/2,webgl0/1,js41/80KB,rm0] V3[entrance-repeats:2]`

That line is an illustration of the format, not numbers to copy. `--verify` recomputes every axis from the page, `DESIGN.md` and the memory log, and rejects the stamp if any number or trace differs. It also rejects bare scores like `C5 H4 S5 R4 M5 V5`, and axes marked `?` (no record to derive from, e.g. `C?[no-record]` when `DESIGN.md` has no Restraint Gate record).

**Any score below 4 → revise before continuing.** Then paste the stamp line gate.mjs printed into the stamp comment:
`/* motomation · archetype: <x> · mutation: <y> · signature: <z> · tier: <n> · critique: <paste> · gate: <paste> */`

The placeholders are deliberate. There are no numbers to copy. Write the archetype, mutation, signature and tier first, because gate.mjs reads them from the comment. Then run `node scripts/gate.mjs <build>` and replace the critique and gate segments with what it printed. Check with `node scripts/gate.mjs --verify <build>`.

---

### Part 2: AI-default scan (every answer must be "no")

**Structure**
1. Is the page hero → logo wall → 3 features → testimonials → pricing → CTA?
2. Is the hero a centred headline + subtitle + two buttons + a screenshot, without a reason?
3. Is there a bento grid without a concept reason?
4. Do all sections use the same layout?
5. Is the nav "logo left, 5 links centre, button right", and the footer four columns of links, without thought?

**Visual**
6. Is the display font <!--rule:banned_display_fonts-->Inter, Roboto, Open Sans, Lato, Poppins, Montserrat, Arial, Helvetica or the system UI stack<!--/rule-->? Is <!--rule:caution_fonts-->Playfair Display and Space Grotesk<!--/rule--> used without a stated reason?
7. Is there a purple/blue/pink gradient, a glowing orb or blurred blobs without meaning?
8. Is glassmorphism used without the concept needing layers?
9. Is there an icon above every feature title?
10. Are there more than one accent colour or more than one display face, without a reason?
11. Is every corner the same large radius, with a shadow and a border all at once?
12. Is the hero image a generic stock photo or AI art with no relation to the brief?

**Content**
13. Is there lorem ipsum, "Acme", "John Doe", or placeholder copy?
14. Are there invented statistics, logos, testimonials or awards?
15. Does the copy contain any banned phrase from `craft/copy.md`?
16. Are there emoji used as icons or bullets?

**Motion**
17. Does anything fade-up on scroll just because it can?
18. Is any animation missing a reduced-motion path?
19. Are layout properties animated?
20. Do UI feedback animations exceed <!--rule:ui_feedback_max_ms-->250ms<!--/rule-->, or use ease-in or `scale(0)` entrances?
21. Is the scroll hijacked (custom scroll that breaks keyboard, anchor links or screen readers)?
22. Does any loop or canvas keep running off-screen?

**Code**
23. Are there TODOs, `// ...rest`, or unfinished components?
24. Are there clickable `div`s, missing labels or missing `alt` text?
25. Are there `markers: true`, console logs or unused imports left in?

**Copy** (the copy pass in `craft/copy.md`)
26. Does more than one section headline share the same shape (all questions, all "X. Y." fragments, all mirror sentences)?
27. Does any sentence end in a vague "-ing" benefit tail, or cite unnamed experts or studies?
28. Is the same thing called by more than one name across the page (synonym cycling)?
29. Does an em dash appear in most paragraphs, or does every section close with a generic invitation?

---

### Part 3: Craft checklist

- [ ] Concept sentence and signature move are visible in the first screen
- [ ] Type: display face chosen with a reason; body ≥ 16px; measure ≤ 75ch; `text-wrap: balance` on headings
- [ ] Colour: all text pairs verified (`node scripts/contrast.mjs` while designing, `node scripts/gate.mjs` on the build), accent ≤ 5% of each screen
- [ ] Layout: one deliberate grid break per screen, recomposed (not squeezed) on mobile
- [ ] Motion: tokens used; `gsap.matchMedia()` with reduced-motion and pointer conditions; `ScrollTrigger.refresh()` after load
- [ ] Mobile motion matrix applied
- [ ] Scroll sequences (pinned, scrubbed, image-sequence, lit-step lists) reviewed per `craft/scroll-sequences.md`, record in the handoff:
  - [ ] Each step's contrast passes AA **active and inactive** (dimmed text measured as rendered: text × opacity + background × (1 − opacity))
  - [ ] Reduced-motion fallback is a **designed still**, not a poster: unpinned plates, every step fully visible
  - [ ] **No step shows a value that is later corrected**
- [ ] Accessibility: keyboard path, visible focus, landmarks, skip link, alt text
- [ ] Performance: LCP image preloaded, heavy libraries loaded dynamically, off-screen work paused
- [ ] SEO: title, description, OG image, structured data, `llms.txt` (for sites)
- [ ] Copy: real, specific, no banned phrases; the copy pass in `craft/copy.md` run with every row "none found" or fixed; `[NEEDS COPY]` markers listed for the user
- [ ] "Restraint Gate record" filled in `DESIGN.md` (concept survived?, every cut, every rejected animation)
- [ ] `node scripts/gate.mjs` run on the build; its full `critique: … · gate: …` line pasted and `--verify` passes (or the exact "not verified — …" line reported: no browser, timed out, or sandbox too constrained)
- [ ] Stamp comment written; run logged with `node scripts/memory.mjs log …`

---

### Handoff note (end every delivery with this)

```
Chose     : <archetype + mutation, signature, type, palette, tier>
Rejected  : <the obvious option and why>
Needs     : <[NEEDS COPY]/[NEEDS ASSET] items for the user>
Measured  : <the gate.mjs stamp line and real numbers, or "not verified — no browser">
Try next  : <one command, e.g. /bolder on the hero, or /motomate the product chapter>
```

<!-- file: commands/critique-format.md -->

## Critique Format

Use this exact structure for `/critique` and for the critique step inside `/overdrive`.

```
CRITIQUE · <page or component>

Scores     C <n> · H <n> · S <n> · R <n> · M <n> · V <n>      (1–5, see gates/delivery-gate.md)
Verdict    <one sentence: the single biggest reason it does or doesn't work>

Top 3 problems (most important first)
1. <problem> — where: <section/file:line> — why it matters: <effect on the user>
   Fix: <specific change>
2. …
3. …

AI-default scan    <n>/25 failed: <list gate numbers>
Motion             <passes / list animations failing the four questions>
Accessibility      <contrast failures with values, keyboard issues, missing reduced-motion>
Performance        <measured numbers, or "not measured">

Keep               <the 1–3 things that are working and must survive the revision>
Next command       <e.g. /mutate hero, /type, /quieter>
```

### Rules

- Be specific: name the element, the value and the fix. "Increase hero display size from 64px to clamp(4rem, 12vw, 14rem)", not "make it bolder".
- Every problem links to a user effect (confusion, slowness, distrust, inaccessibility, forgettability).
- Never invent measurements. If you didn't measure performance, say so.
- Always include **Keep**. Critique protects what works.


---

<!-- file: commands/overview.md -->

## Commands

Type a command at the start of a message. Commands combine with flags. Without a command, the skill runs `/build` when the request is to create something, and `/critique` when it's to review.

### Flags (work with every command)

| Flag | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `--tier` | 1–5 | Force a motion tier |
| `--energy` `--rhythm` `--motion` | 1–3 | Set a dial (see `principles/dials.md`) |
| `--mood` | quiet · editorial · play | Set all three dials from a preset |
| `--style` | a file in `styles/` | Apply a visual language |
| `--stack` | next · react · vanilla · astro | Target framework (default: detect, else Next.js) |
| `--seed` | any number | Repeatable collision draws |
| `--review` | — | Stop after the preview block and wait for approval |

---

### Create

#### `/shape [brief]`
**What:** turns a brief into a design direction without code: brief inference, the Thinking Sequence, dials, and a `DESIGN.md` + `MOTION.md`.
**When:** at the very start, or when the client must approve a direction first.
**Output:** preview block + `DESIGN.md` + `MOTION.md` (from `templates/`).

#### `/build [brief]`
**What:** the full flow, from brief to finished, gated code.
**When:** you want a complete page or site.
**Output:** preview block → complete code → Delivery Gate scores → handoff note.

#### `/invent [topic]`
**What:** runs the collision engine (`scripts/collide.mjs --n 3 --spread`; `--count N` for more) and proposes **three different concepts**, each with tension, concept, type mode (HOUSE STYLE or SERVICE STYLE, with the reason from the brief), archetype + mutation, collision and signature.
**Guarantees (enforced by the script, reported in its "Diversity (measured)" block):** the three draws never share an archetype or a signature seed; mutations and collision worlds don't repeat either while their pools last (12 mutations, 20 archetypes, 22 signature seeds). When `--count` asks for more than a pool holds, the script says which pool ran out and from which draw repeats start; it never overlaps silently. Copy that block into the output. Without a shell, draw by hand and state that uniqueness was checked by eye.
**When:** you're stuck, or the first idea feels familiar.
**Output:** three concept cards plus the measured diversity line. Pick one and continue with `/build`.

#### `/signature [section]`
**What:** invents one signature move for the site or a section, bent from `signatures/` to the concept.
**When:** the page works but nobody will remember it.
**Output:** the move in recipe format (idea, why, build, detail, off-switch, prompt) and its implementation.

#### `/motomate [section]`
**What:** turns a section into a Tier 5 scroll-film: storyboard in `MOTION.md`, technique choice (DOM, image sequence, video, WebGL), asset pipeline, code and fallbacks.
**When:** a product, place or story should play like a film as you scroll.
**Output:** storyboard table + ffmpeg commands (if needed) + code + static fallback.

#### `/animate [target] --tier=n`
**What:** adds motion to existing UI at the given tier, following the four questions.
**When:** the design is done but static.
**Output:** a motion plan (what moves, why, tokens) + code.

#### `/type [target]`
**What:** a typography pass: face choice with reasons, fluid scale, tracking, wrapping, numerals, variable-axis opportunities.
**When:** the page feels generic, and the type is usually why.

---

### Tune

#### `/bolder [target]`
Raises ENERGY by one step: bigger type jumps, stronger contrast, a braver accent moment, one more grid break. Keeps the concept.

#### `/quieter [target]`
Lowers ENERGY and/or MOTION by one step: more air, fewer moving parts, softer accent, slower reveals.

#### `/distill [target]`
Removes until only the essential remains. Runs the Restraint Gate hard: one signature, one accent, fewer sections.

#### `/mutate [target]`
Keeps the content and concept but changes the **structure**: a different archetype or mutation, drawn with `collide.mjs`. Use it when the layout feels like a template.

#### `/overdrive [target]`
A generate → critique → improve loop, up to 3 rounds. Each round scores the six critique axes and fixes the lowest one. Stops when every axis is 4 or more. Use it for flagship pages.

---

### Evaluate

#### `/critique [target or URL]`
A design review in the format of `commands/critique-format.md`: scores, the three most important problems, and fixes in priority order. Doesn't change code unless asked.

#### `/audit [target]`
A technical gate: accessibility, performance, reduced motion, mobile matrix, SEO and the AI-default scan. Returns pass/fail per item with file and line references.

#### `/study [reference URL or screenshot]`
Extracts the **design DNA** of a reference **without copying it**, and writes it into `DESIGN.md` as a "Studied direction" in five sections: type, palette, layout, motion, signature. It ends with what to take (decisions) and what to leave (anything that would make a copy). Agent-driven: the agent opens the URL or reads the screenshot, and no script fetches anything. Measured values are marked as measured, and missing evidence as `not observed`. Full input, output and rules: `commands/study.md`.

---

### Ship

#### `/polish [target]`
The final pass: spacing rhythm, alignment, typographic details (quotes, dashes, numerals), focus states, hover/press states, empty and error states, loading, favicon and OG image, the stamp comment and the memory log.

---

### Meta

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/dials` | Shows the current dials and tier, or sets them: `/dials energy=3 motion=2` |
| `/help` | Lists commands with one-line descriptions and suggests the next step |
| `/version` | Prints the installed version from `VERSION` |
| `/check-update` | Compares the installed version with the latest on GitHub (see `commands/update.md`) |
| `/update-skill` | Explains how to update: `npx skills update asfakulsiam-motomation-design` |

### Typical sequences

- New site: `/shape` → approve → `/build` → `/critique` → `/polish`
- Stuck on ideas: `/invent` → pick → `/build --review`
- Existing site feels generic: `/critique` → `/mutate` → `/type` → `/signature`
- Product launch: `/shape --mood=play` → `/motomate hero-product` → `/audit`


---

<!-- file: commands/study.md -->

## `/study [url | screenshot]`

**What:** reads an existing page (a URL the agent opens, or a screenshot the user attaches) and writes its **design direction** into `DESIGN.md`, in five sections: type, palette, layout, motion, signature. It studies how the page makes its decisions so a new design can learn from it. It doesn't clone the page.

**When:**
- The client says "like this site".
- You inherit a page and need its system written down before `/redesign`.
- A reference needs to be checked against the anti-sameness rules before you borrow from it.

### Input

- **URL:** the agent opens it with whatever browsing or browser tool it has. `/study` itself fetches nothing and runs no script against the URL. If the agent can't open pages, ask for a screenshot.
- **Screenshot:** one or more images. Desktop and 375px views give the best read. Without a 375px view, mark the responsive part as `not observed`.
- **Optional:** `--section <name>` to study one part only (hero, nav, a pinned chapter).

### Output

A `DESIGN.md` built from `templates/DESIGN.md`, with a **Studied direction** block at the top:

```markdown
### Studied direction
- Source: <url or "screenshot, <date>">, studied <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Read by: <how: live page with computed styles | screenshot only>

#### Type
Families (display / text / mono) and how you know (computed style, or "looks like" for screenshots), scale ratio, weights, tracking, case, the one typographic decision that carries the page.

#### Palette
Ground, surface, ink, muted, accent as hex values (sampled, not guessed). Contrast of ink/ground and accent/ground, from `scripts/contrast.mjs` where a shell exists. Where the accent is used and where it isn't.

#### Layout
Grid and margins, section rhythm, nav pattern, the closest archetype from `structures/archetypes.md`, and what breaks the grid on purpose.

#### Motion
Motion tier (1–5) and the evidence for it (transitions, scroll-linked effects, pinning, WebGL), the easing and duration feel, and what happens under reduced motion (`not observed` if you couldn't test it).

#### Signature
The one moment people remember, described as a concept in this skill's vocabulary (`references/effects-vocabulary.md`). Say whether it serves the page's idea or decorates it.

#### What to take / what to leave
Two short lists. "Take" holds decisions, never assets. "Leave" names what would make a new design read as a copy.
```

### Rules

1. **Direction, not assets.** Don't copy logos, photographs, illustrations, copy, code or font files. Fonts are named, not downloaded. Commercial faces get an alternative from `data/fonts.csv`.
2. **Measure what you can, label what you can't.** Live page: read computed styles and sample colours. Screenshot: say "looks like" for fonts, sample hex values from the pixels, and mark motion as `not observed`.
3. **Every section is filled.** Write `not observed` when evidence is missing. Never guess silently.
4. **Study, then diverge.** A studied direction is a starting point. Before `/build`, run the Thinking Sequence's anti-sameness step against it, so the new page shares at most two of: layout family, type pairing, palette, signature.
5. **Credit the source** in the Studied direction block.
6. **No automatic fetching.** `/study` is agent-driven: the agent decides to open the page and records what it saw. No script in this skill requests the URL.

## Updating

### Check the installed version
Read `VERSION` in the skill folder. `/version` prints it.

### Check for a newer version
Compare with the latest release:
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asfakulsiam/asfakulsiam-motomation-design/main/skills/asfakulsiam-motomation-design/VERSION
```
If the remote version is higher, tell the user and show the update command. Don't update automatically.

### Update
```bash
npx skills update asfakulsiam-motomation-design        # project install
npx skills update asfakulsiam-motomation-design -g     # global install
```
Claude Code plugin users: `/plugin marketplace update asfakulsiam-motomation-design`.
Chat tools (ChatGPT, Grok, Google AI Studio, v0, Lovable): download the new `dist/motomation-design.md` and replace the old file in your project or instructions.

After updating, read `CHANGELOG.md` in the repository for what changed.

<!-- file: adapters/astro.md -->

## Adapter: Astro

- Content-first and zero-JS by default, so it's great for editorial sites and SEO.
- Put motion in a `<script>` inside the component (bundled and deduplicated), or in a framework island (`client:visible`) for React components.
- Cross-document View Transitions: `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` in global CSS, or Astro's `<ClientRouter />`. With the client router, re-initialise GSAP on `astro:page-load` and kill triggers on `astro:before-swap`.
- Fonts with Astro's font API or `@fontsource-variable/*`.


---

<!-- file: adapters/next.md -->

## Adapter: Next.js (App Router)

```bash
npm i gsap @gsap/react lenis
```

- Motion components are client components (`"use client"`). Keep pages and layouts as server components, and pass content down as props, so text is server-rendered for SEO.
- Fonts: `next/font/google` or `next/font/local`, exposed as CSS variables:
  ```ts
  import { Fraunces, Inter_Tight } from "next/font/google";
  const display = Fraunces({ subsets: ["latin"], axes: ["SOFT", "WONK", "opsz"], variable: "--font-display" });
  ```
- Register GSAP plugins once in a client module (`lib/gsap.ts`) and import from there.
- Smooth scroll: a client `<SmoothScroll>` provider in `app/layout.tsx` using `ReactLenis` with `autoRaf: false`, driven by `gsap.ticker`. See `examples/providers/smooth-scroll.tsx`.
- Route changes: call `ScrollTrigger.refresh()` after the new page mounts; `useGSAP` reverts the old page's triggers on unmount.
- Images: `next/image` with `sizes` and `priority` on the LCP image. Image sequences live in `/public/film/…` and are drawn to a canvas (no `next/image`).
- Three.js: `dynamic(() => import("./Scene"), { ssr: false })`.
- Metadata: export `metadata` / `generateMetadata` per route, plus `app/opengraph-image.tsx`, `app/sitemap.ts`, `app/robots.ts` and `public/llms.txt`.

| Platform | How to use the skill | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, Cline, Roo, Kiro, OpenCode, Goose, Junie, Zed, Amp** and other skills-compatible agents | `npx skills add asfakulsiam/asfakulsiam-motomation-design` | The agent loads `SKILL.md` and reads the other files on demand. Scripts run in the terminal |
| **Claude Code (plugin)** | `/plugin marketplace add asfakulsiam/asfakulsiam-motomation-design`, then `/plugin install asfakulsiam-motomation-design@asfakulsiam-motomation-design` | Same skill, managed as a plugin |
| **Claude.ai / Claude Desktop** | Upload the skill folder as a zip under Settings → Capabilities → Skills (where available), or attach `dist/motomation-design.md` to a Project | Without a shell, it uses the CSV data directly |
| **ChatGPT** | Add `dist/motomation-design.md` to a Project's files or a custom GPT's knowledge, and add "Follow motomation-design.md for every web design task" to the instructions | Use the single-file prompts in `signatures/` |
| **Grok, Google AI Studio, Gemini app** | Paste `dist/motomation-design.md` into the system instructions, or attach it to the conversation or project | Ask for one `index.html` using `adapters/vanilla.md` |
| **v0, Lovable, Bolt, Replit Agent** | Add the content of `dist/motomation-design.md` to the project's knowledge, rules or custom instructions | Name the stack these tools use (Next.js / React + Tailwind) |

### Without a shell

When scripts can't run:
1. **Collisions:** use the seed method in `invention/mad-artist.md` with the CSVs in `data/`.
2. **Search:** read the relevant CSV and choose deliberately. Never take the first row.
3. **Memory:** ask the user to keep the stamp comment. Check stamps in the code they paste back.
4. **Contrast:** calculate WCAG contrast manually, or ask the user to verify with any contrast checker.

<!-- file: adapters/react-vite.md -->

## Adapter: React + Vite

```bash
npm create vite@latest site -- --template react-ts && cd site && npm i gsap @gsap/react lenis
```

- Use `useGSAP(() => …, { scope })` for every animation; it handles cleanup on unmount and in Strict Mode.
- Smooth scroll provider at the root, as in the Next adapter (no `"use client"` needed).
- Pre-render marketing pages (e.g. `vite-plugin-ssg`, or move to Astro/Next) if SEO matters. A client-only SPA hides content from crawlers until JS runs.
- Self-host fonts with `@fontsource-variable/<family>` packages where available.
- Code-split heavy scenes with `React.lazy(() => import("./Scene"))`.


---

<!-- file: adapters/vanilla.md -->

## Adapter: Plain HTML / CSS / JS

The most portable route: works in any host, and in chat tools that can only produce one file.

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3/dist/gsap.min.js" defer></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3/dist/ScrollTrigger.min.js" defer></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3/dist/SplitText.min.js" defer></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lenis@1/dist/lenis.min.js" defer></script>
```

- Pin versions in production (e.g. `gsap@3.15.0`) and self-host if you can.
- Add `class="js"` to `<html>` in an inline script, so CSS can hide static fallbacks only when JS runs.
- Wrap all motion in `gsap.matchMedia()` exactly as in the framework examples.
- A complete single-file reference lives in `examples/html/motomation-film.html`.

## Effects Vocabulary

A shared language for effects, so a designer and an agent mean the same thing. Each entry is a **concept**, described in this skill's own words, with the tier it needs and when it earns its place. The **In this skill** column points to this skill's own component (`examples/components/`, catalogue in `examples/components/README.md`), signature or example. Everything referenced here was written for this skill.

Find before build (see `SKILL.md`, step 6): for a standard effect, check the project's own components first, then this table and the component library, before writing it from scratch. The signature move is never swapped for a ready-made effect.

### Text effects

| Concept | What it does | Tier | Earns its place when | In this skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Line rise | Lines slide up from behind masks | 2 | Default editorial reveal | `examples/animation/line-curtain.tsx` |
| Blur focus | Words sharpen from blur into focus | 2 | The concept is about clarity or focus | `examples/components/type/blur-focus.tsx` |
| Decode | Characters resolve from random glyphs | 2 | Technical, secret or data-led brands; short labels only | signature `decode` · `examples/components/type/decode.tsx` |
| Proximity weight | Weight/width follows cursor distance | 2 | Type-led identities; one word only | signature `proximity-weight` in `signatures/type-signatures.md` · `examples/typography/proximity-weight.tsx` |
| Pressure type | Letters stretch or compress toward the cursor | 2 | Playful, elastic brands | `examples/components/type/pressure-type.tsx` |
| Scroll float | Letters bob into place as they scroll in | 2 | Play mood display lines | `examples/components/type/scroll-float.tsx` |
| Ink fill | Words fill from muted to ink while reading | 2 | Manifestos, about statements | signature `ink-fill` · `examples/components/type/ink-fill.tsx` |
| Velocity type | Text skews or widens with scroll speed | 2 | Sport, speed, launches | signature `velocity-skew` · `examples/components/scroll/velocity-marquee.tsx` · `examples/components/type/width-sprint.tsx` |
| Split-flap | Characters flip like a departure board | 2 | Schedules, menus, travel | `examples/components/type/split-flap.tsx` |
| Curved text | Text runs along a circle or path | 1–2 | Badges, stamps, seals | `examples/components/type/curved-text.tsx` |
| Text gradient sweep | A highlight runs across the text | 1 | A single key word, rarely | concept only (CSS `background-clip: text` with a moving gradient; one word) |
| Type film | A headline choreographed across a pinned chapter | 5 | Motomation hooks | `motion/tier-5-motomation.md` · `examples/html/motomation-film.html` |
| Neighbour moves | Each letter of a name has its own small move on hover, so the word feels like a cast | 2 | Play-mood names and logotypes of 3–12 letters | `examples/components/type/neighbour-moves.tsx` |
| Letter relay | The hero name shrinks and travels into the header letter by letter as the first screen scrolls away | 2 | The name is the identity (portfolios, personal brands) | `examples/components/type/letter-relay.tsx` |

### Backgrounds and atmosphere

| Concept | What it does | Tier | Earns its place when | In this skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grain | Animated or static film noise | 1–2 | Analogue, photographic or warm moods | `examples/components/backgrounds/grain.tsx` |
| Liquid field | Flowing colour like silk or ink in water | 4 | The material is liquid, fabric or light | `examples/components/backgrounds/liquid-field.tsx` |
| Dot / grid field | A grid of dots or lines that reacts to the cursor | 2–4 | Technical, structural concepts | `examples/components/backgrounds/dot-field.tsx` |
| Aurora / light bands | Soft moving light | 4 | Night, sky, northern brands. Overused, needs a strong reason | `examples/components/backgrounds/light-sweep.tsx` (one band) · `motion/tier-4-max.md` |
| Dither / halftone | Images rendered as print dots | 2–4 | Print, retro, newspaper concepts | `examples/components/backgrounds/halftone.tsx` |
| Particles / galaxy | Fields of points in space | 4 | Space, data or scale concepts. Usually decoration | `motion/tier-4-max.md` |
| Shader distortion | Images ripple or bend on hover/scroll | 4 | Water, heat, memory | `motion/tier-4-max.md` |
| Contour lines | Topographic lines that drift slowly, like a map breathing | 2 | Land, climate, outdoors and mapping stories | `examples/components/backgrounds/contour-lines.tsx` |

### Cursor and interaction

| Concept | What it does | Tier | Earns its place when | In this skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Image trail | Images spawn along the cursor path | 2 | Photographers, archives | `examples/components/cursor/image-trail.tsx` |
| Pixel wake | Pixel squares trail the cursor | 2 | Digital, pixel, retro concepts | signature `pixel-wake` · `examples/components/cursor/pixel-wake.tsx` |
| Lens | A circle reveals an alternate layer | 2 | Before/after, sketch/final, day/night | signature `lens` · `examples/components/cursor/lens.tsx` |
| Magnet | Elements lean toward the cursor | 2 | 1–2 primary actions only | signature `considerate-magnet` in `signatures/cursor-and-micro-signatures.md` · `examples/micro-interactions/magnetic-button.tsx` |
| Target cursor | The cursor locks to interactive elements | 2 | Precision tools, games | `examples/components/cursor/target-cursor.tsx` |
| Splash / fluid cursor | The cursor stirs a fluid simulation | 4 | Liquid concepts only | `motion/tier-4-max.md` (Tier 4 only) |
| Tilt card | Cards rotate in 3D toward the cursor | 2 | Physical objects (cards, tickets, products) | `examples/components/cursor/tilt-card.tsx` |
| Seismograph line | A hairline divider bends toward the cursor and springs back with a small wobble | 2 | One living detail on a calm editorial page; sound and measurement brands | `examples/components/cursor/seismograph-line.tsx` |

### Scroll

| Concept | What it does | Tier | Earns its place when | In this skill |

| Reading rail | A thin rail fills as you read the article | 1 | Long reads and documentation | `examples/components/scroll/reading-rail.tsx` |

| Flowing menu | Menu items reveal a marquee image on hover | 2 | Portfolio and studio navigation | `examples/components/layout/flowing-menu.tsx` |
| Dock | Icons magnify near the cursor | 2 | App-like tool collections | `examples/components/layout/dock.tsx` |

### Micro-interactions

| Concept | What it does | Tier | Earns its place when | In this skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hold to commit | Press and hold fills, then confirms | 1–2 | Important, irreversible actions | signature `hold-to-commit` · `examples/components/micro/hold-to-commit.tsx` |
| Count-up | Numbers count to their value | 2 | Real figures with sources only | `examples/components/micro/count-up.tsx` |

Use this vocabulary in briefs and critiques: "Replace the aurora background with a grain + lens concept tied to the darkroom idea."
| Remembered list | Links you have opened get a quiet tick, remembered on this device | 1 | Archives, project lists and course modules people return to | `examples/components/micro/remembered-list.tsx` |

<!-- file: references/gsap-lenis.md -->

## GSAP + Lenis Quick Reference

### Imports
```js
import gsap from "gsap";
import { ScrollTrigger } from "gsap/ScrollTrigger";
import { SplitText } from "gsap/SplitText";
import { Flip } from "gsap/Flip";
import { useGSAP } from "@gsap/react";
import Lenis from "lenis";
gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, SplitText, Flip, useGSAP);
```

### ScrollTrigger options you'll use most
| Option | Typical |
|---|---|
| `start` / `end` | `"top 80%"`, `"top top"`, `"+=300%"`, `() => "+=" + el.offsetWidth` |
| `scrub` | `true` (exact) or `0.5–1.5` (weight) |
| `pin` | `true`; add `anticipatePin: 1` for fast scrollers |
| `once` | `true` for reveals that shouldn't replay |
| `toggleActions` | `"play none none reverse"` for non-scrubbed reveals |
| `invalidateOnRefresh` | `true` when values are functions of layout |
| `containerAnimation` | animate items inside a horizontal pinned track |

### Lifecycle
- React: `useGSAP` with `{ scope }`; everything is reverted on unmount.
- Vanilla: `const ctx = gsap.context(() => {...}, root); ctx.revert();`
- Responsive and reduced motion: `gsap.matchMedia()`, which reverts automatically when queries change.
- After fonts/images: `document.fonts.ready.then(() => ScrollTrigger.refresh())`.

### Lenis
```js
const lenis = new Lenis({ autoRaf: false, lerp: 0.1 });    // smaller lerp = smoother and slower
lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update);
gsap.ticker.add((t) => lenis.raf(t * 1000));
gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0);
// anchor links: lenis.scrollTo("#section", { offset: -80 })
// stop during modals: lenis.stop(); lenis.start();
```
Lenis respects `prefers-reduced-motion` by default and keeps native touch scrolling unless you set `syncTouch: true` (don't, for most sites). Add `data-lenis-prevent` to scrollable inner panels.

### Debugging
- `markers: true` during development only.
- `ScrollTrigger.getAll()` to list triggers; `ScrollTrigger.killAll()` in hot-reload edge cases.
- If pinned sections jump: check for CSS `transform` on ancestors, and fonts loading after measurement.

## Inspiration and Resource Libraries

Use these to **study**, not to copy. Run `/study <url>` to extract principles.

| Need | Go to |
|---|---|
| Award-level sites to study | awwwards.com, thefwa.com, cssdesignawards.com, godly.website, siteinspire.com |
| Motion and scroll references | gsap.com/showcase, codepen.io (search "ScrollTrigger"), lenis.darkroom.engineering |
| Effect components | this skill's own library: `examples/components/` (catalogue in its README, live demos in `examples/gallery/index.html`) |
| Small interaction ideas with prompts | github.com/miguelclavel/interaction-recipes |
| Type | fonts.google.com, fontshare.com, pangrampangram.com, typewolf.com, fontsinuse.com |
| Colour | coolors.co, oklch.com, huemint.com, realtimecolors.com |
| 3D and shaders | threejs.org/examples, shadertoy.com, thebookofshaders.com |
| Illustrated motion | lottiefiles.com, rive.app/community |
| Accessibility checks | webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker, wave.webaim.org |
| Performance checks | pagespeed.web.dev, web.dev/articles/vitals |

### Rules for using references
1. Collect three references from **outside** the category (a hotel brief studies a bookshop, a film title and a museum).
2. Extract principles: what is the structure, the type logic, the motion language?
3. Never copy a layout, illustration or code wholesale. Check the license before using any asset or code.
